facts.statement: Dromicosuchus fossils were found in Upper Triassic rocks in North Carolina, United States.
facts.quote: It was found in Upper Triassic rocks of North Carolina, United States

facts.statement: The genus Dromicosuchus was named and described by Hans-Dieter Sues and colleagues in 2003.
facts.quote: It was named and described by Hans-Dieter Sues and colleagues in 2003.

facts.statement: The type species D. grallator means "one who walks on stilts" in Latin, referring to the animal's long and slender limbs.
facts.quote: The type species is D. grallator, meaning "one who walks on stilts" in Latin, in reference to its long slender limbs.

facts.statement: Dromicosuchus is estimated to have been between 1.2 and 1.3 meters long.
facts.quote: The animal is estimated as 1.2 to 1.3 m long.

facts.statement: The skull of Dromicosuchus was lightly built, triangular, and approximately 150 mm long.
facts.quote: The skull was lightly built and triangular, and about 150 mm long from the snout to the forward-most part of the occipital margin.

facts.statement: The third or fourth tooth in the lower jaw of Dromicosuchus was notably enlarged and fit into a notch in the upper jaw.
facts.quote: The third or fourth tooth of the lower jaw was notably enlarged, fitting into a notch in the upper jaw between the premaxilla and maxilla.

facts.statement: The left forearm of Dromicosuchus was noticeably longer than its upper arm, measuring 102 mm compared to 89 mm.
facts.quote: The left upper arm was 89 mm long, and left ulna was 102 mm long, so the forearm was noticeably longer than the upper arm.

facts.statement: The left hindlimb of Dromicosuchus had a thigh bone 144 mm long and a shin bone 130 mm long.
facts.quote: For the left hindlimb, the thigh bone was 144 mm long and the shin was 130 mm long.

facts.statement: A Dromicosuchus specimen was found beneath a larger rauisuchian with bite damage, suggesting it was attacked by the predator before both died and were buried.
facts.quote: This specimen is unusual in that it was found beneath the skeleton of a larger rauisuchian (Postosuchus alisonae) and has apparent bite damage, suggesting that it was attacked by the larger carnivore before both died and were buried together.

facts.statement: Gut contents of the rauisuchian found with Dromicosuchus included bones from an aetosaur, a cynodont, a dicynodont, and a possible temnospondyl.
facts.quote: these included bones and scutes of the aetosaur Stegomus, some with tooth marks; bones from the snout, arm, and shoulder of the traversodont cynodont Plinthogomphodon; phalanx bones of a dicynodont; and a bone fragment from a possible temnospondyl.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis groups Dromicosuchus as a sphenosuchian, possibly closest to Hesperosuchus and Kayentasuchus.
facts.quote: Sues and his colleagues performed a phylogenetic analysis and found that their new genus (identified as Dromaeosuchus in the diagrams) grouped as a sphenosuchian, possibly closest to Hesperosuchus and Kayentasuchus.

facts.statement: Dromicosuchus lived during the Carnian to Norian stages, approximately 237 to 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Norian (237 to 205.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: Dromicosuchus belongs to the parent group Crocodylomorpha.
Dromicosuchus is classified within the class Reptilia.
